subject: CHEMISTRY

subtopics.title: Reaction observations and balanced equations

slots.X: A carbon sample burns in an open dish and the remaining ash weighs less than the original carbon. Construct two possible carbon–oxygen product ledgers and identify which gas and residue measurements would distinguish complete oxidation from incomplete combustion. Explain why the open-dish mass is not a conservation test.
slots.Y: Atoms are conserved in chemical reactions; balanced equations count participating chemical entities, while observations alone do not establish product identity.
slots.Z: If carbon converts completely to carbon dioxide, C + O₂ → CO₂, gas leaves the open dish and the residual ash mass is not the total product mass. Limited oxygen may also permit 2C + O₂ → 2CO or retained carbon. Measure evolved gas composition and residual carbon in a closed material balance before identifying the pathway. Both candidate equations conserve carbon and oxygen atoms.
slots.W: Select the material-system boundary, distinguish CO₂ formation from possible CO or unreacted carbon, and design measurements needed to decide between the ledgers.

Construct two possible carbon–oxygen product ledgers and identify which gas and residue measurements would distinguish complete oxidation from incomplete combustion. qrt_instances.wrong_idea: A lighter ash proves carbon atoms were destroyed.
qrt_instances.replacement_rule: Avoid: A lighter ash proves carbon atoms were destroyed. Instead demonstrate the claim with balanced species and observations.

qrt_instances.independent_check: If gas collection is incomplete, determine which mass conclusions can still be made without assuming all carbon became CO₂.

slots.Z: The reactants have four Mg and four O atoms. Four MgO formula units conserve both, so the particle ratio is 4 Mg + 2 O₂ → 4 MgO, the same reaction as 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO in simplest whole-number coefficients.

Construct a balanced product sketch and symbolic reaction without changing molecular subscripts. Check the changed condition: If only two Mg atoms react, what remains from the original sketch?

slots.Z: No. White appearance is not unique evidence. Compare source metal identity, oxygen consumption in a closed apparatus, mass changes and independent residue tests. Atom conservation constrains candidate equations but does not establish product chemistry without species evidence.

subtopics.title: Combination and decomposition

slots.X: Explain why melting ice and thermal decomposition of CaCO₃ must be classified differently even though both need energy.
slots.Y: Combination and decomposition depend on reactant/product species changes, not merely heating or visible colour changes.
slots.Z: Ice melting is H₂O(s) → H₂O(l), a state change with unchanged molecular species. CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g) creates new chemical species. Energy input alone is not the deciding criterion.
slots.W: Independently explain the decisive model for this exact case: Explain why melting ice and thermal decomposition of CaCO₃ must be classified differently even though both need energy. Check the changed condition: Can one classify a process simply from a temperature rise?

subtopics.title: Single and double displacement

slots.X: Explain why Zn deposits copper from CuSO₄ but Cu ordinarily does not displace zinc from ZnSO₄.
slots.Y: Displacement requires chemical feasibility; symbol exchange is not proof of reaction.
slots.Z: Zinc is more reactive in these conditions, and Zn atoms can form Zn²⁺ while reducing Cu²⁺ to copper metal. The reverse process is not favoured in ordinary aqueous conditions. The observed reddish deposit alone still merits confirmation.
slots.W: Independently explain the decisive model for this exact case: Explain why Zn deposits copper from CuSO₄ but Cu ordinarily does not displace zinc from ZnSO₄. Check the changed condition: Could a missing deposit be due to a dirty or coated zinc surface?

qrt_instances.student_task: Explain why Zn deposits copper from CuSO₄ but Cu ordinarily does not displace zinc from ZnSO₄.
qrt_instances.wrong_idea: 'Swap ions or metals in an equation and a reaction must occur' confuses a formal writing operation with chemical feasibility. Repair by checking observed species, energy/reactivity conditions, soluble products and controls.
qrt_instances.replacement_rule: 'Swap ions or metals in an equation and a reaction must occur' confuses a formal writing operation with chemical feasibility. Repair by checking observed species, energy/reactivity conditions, soluble products and controls.

slots.X: A clean Zn strip loses 0.010 mol Zn into AgNO₃(aq), while only 0.018 mol metallic Ag is collected. Write the net ionic reaction and electron ledger; calculate the ideal silver deposition and identify two measurements needed to account for the discrepancy.
slots.Y: Displacement requires chemical feasibility; symbol exchange is not proof of reaction.
slots.Z: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻, while 2Ag⁺ + 2e⁻ → 2Ag. Therefore Zn(s) + 2Ag⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s); nitrate is spectator. A 0.010 mol Zn loss could support 0.020 mol Ag if that is the sole process and Ag⁺ is sufficient. The 0.018 mol collected leaves 0.002 mol difference, but cannot alone identify whether Ag detached, other reductions occurred, or collection was incomplete. Test remaining Ag⁺ and recover filtered solids.
slots.W: Use Zn/Ag electron stoichiometry to calculate the independently expected Ag amount, then evaluate alternative explanations for an incomplete recovered deposit.

subtopics.title: Precipitation and aqueous reaction evidence

slots.X: Mix 0.010 mol Ca(NO₃)₂(aq) with 0.006 mol Na₂CO₃(aq). Construct the net ionic precipitation equation, find the maximum solid amount and the leftover calcium-ion amount, and explain why a white precipitate alone cannot prove its formula.
slots.Y: Precipitation is formation of an insoluble solid, but cloudiness alone does not uniquely identify it.
slots.Z: Ca²⁺(aq) + CO₃²⁻(aq) → CaCO₃(s). Each mole of carbonate consumes one mole Ca²⁺, so carbonate limits and at most 0.006 mol CaCO₃ forms; 0.004 mol calcium ion remains, assuming complete precipitation and no other processes. Sodium and nitrate remain in solution. White appearance alone cannot uniquely identify CaCO₃; independent composition tests are needed.
slots.W: Find the limiting precipitating ion, keep sodium/nitrate as spectators, and separate a stoichiometric prediction from chemical identity evidence.

qrt_instances.student_task: Mix 0.010 mol Ca(NO₃)₂(aq) with 0.006 mol Na₂CO₃(aq). Construct the net ionic precipitation equation, find the maximum solid amount and the leftover calcium-ion amount, and explain why a white precipitate alone cannot prove its formula.
qrt_instances.wrong_idea: All dissolved calcium disappears once any cloudy solid appears.
qrt_instances.replacement_rule: Avoid: All dissolved calcium disappears once any cloudy solid appears. Instead demonstrate the claim with balanced species and observations.
qrt_instances.visual_job: Show an accurate Chemistry diagram or evidence table for aqueous ions, solubility and turbidity, with the decisive result unmarked.
qrt_instances.independent_check: Suppose only 0.003 mol carbonate was actually added. What can be calculated and what remains experimentally uncertain?

slots.X: Two clear solutions identified as AgNO₃(aq) and KBr(aq) produce a pale solid. Draw before/after ionic inventories, identify the spectator ions, and propose a chemical measurement that could distinguish the proposed AgBr solid from a visually similar contaminant.
slots.Y: Precipitation is formation of an insoluble solid, but cloudiness alone does not uniquely identify it.
slots.Z: Ag⁺ + Br⁻ → AgBr(s) is the expected net ionic equation for the stated solutions. Potassium and nitrate remain dissolved; the solution inventory must conserve each element and overall charge. Appearance does not establish that the isolated solid is pure AgBr. Confirm its constituents with suitable independent analysis and controlled blanks rather than assigning composition by colour alone.
slots.W: Independently translate the Ag⁺/Br⁻ reaction into a complete ion ledger and distinguish evidence of precipitation from proof of the solid's identity.

qrt_instances.replacement_rule: Avoid: A pale precipitate uniquely determines its chemical composition. Instead demonstrate the claim with balanced species and observations.

subtopics.title: Exothermic and endothermic changes

slots.X: Explain why an exothermic reaction can need initial heating before it starts and why the vessel may warm afterward.
slots.Y: Exothermic/endothermic refer to system energy change, not necessarily a single observed thermometer reading.
slots.Z: An activation barrier must be crossed for the reaction to proceed. Once it proceeds, the final reaction energy is lower than the starting energy under an exothermic model, releasing heat to surroundings. Barrier and net energy change are distinct.
slots.W: Independently explain the decisive model for this exact case: Explain why an exothermic reaction can need initial heating before it starts and why the vessel may warm afterward. Check the changed condition: Can an endothermic process also require an activation barrier?

subtopics.title: Oxidation/reduction qualitative introduction

slots.X: Consider the idealised net reaction Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Use both oxygen-transfer and oxidation-number models to decide what is oxidised and reduced, and explain which evidence would be needed to show the iron oxide was actually converted.
slots.Y: Oxidation and reduction occur together, with oxygen transfer one useful school-level model.
slots.Z: Fe₂O₃ loses oxygen and is reduced to Fe, whereas CO gains oxygen and is oxidised to CO₂. Fe is formally +3 in Fe₂O₃ and 0 in Fe; carbon rises from +2 in CO to +4 in CO₂. Three carbon atoms each lose 2 e⁻ while two iron ions each gain 3 e⁻, so 6 electrons balance. Product iron and gas identity require measurements; a dark-to-grey appearance alone cannot prove complete conversion.
slots.W: Use paired oxygen and electron ledgers for iron oxide/carbon monoxide and distinguish balanced possibility from verified conversion.

qrt_instances.student_task: Consider the idealised net reaction Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Use both oxygen-transfer and oxidation-number models to decide what is oxidised and reduced, and explain which evidence would be needed to show the iron oxide was actually converted.
qrt_instances.wrong_idea: Oxidation means a substance must react with O₂ gas, so CO cannot be oxidised here.
qrt_instances.replacement_rule: Avoid: Oxidation means a substance must react with O₂ gas, so CO cannot be oxidised here. Instead demonstrate the claim with balanced species and observations.
qrt_instances.visual_job: Show an accurate Chemistry diagram or evidence table for oxygen or electron exchange, with the decisive result unmarked.
qrt_instances.independent_check: What if the solid contains both Fe and unreacted Fe₂O₃? Does the net equation alone establish conversion fraction?

slots.X: A zinc strip contacts a solution containing Pb²⁺ and solid lead appears under controlled conditions. Write both half-reactions and the net ionic equation. Explain why the process is redox even though no oxygen moves.
slots.Y: Oxidation and reduction occur together, with oxygen transfer one useful school-level model.
slots.Z: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ and Pb²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Pb. The sum Zn(s) + Pb²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Pb(s) conserves atoms and net charge +2. Zinc is oxidised and lead ions reduced even though no oxygen species appears. This demonstrates the limits of the oxygen-transfer-only introductory definition.
slots.W: Infer oxidation and reduction from electron transfer in an oxygen-free metal-ion displacement; preserve net ionic charge and atom balance.

qrt_instances.student_task: A zinc strip contacts a solution containing Pb²⁺ and solid lead appears under controlled conditions. Write both half-reactions and the net ionic equation. Explain why the process is redox even though no oxygen moves.
qrt_instances.wrong_idea: No oxygen occurs in the equation, so oxidation is impossible.
qrt_instances.replacement_rule: Avoid: No oxygen occurs in the equation, so oxidation is impossible. Instead demonstrate the claim with balanced species and observations.
qrt_instances.visual_job: Show an accurate Chemistry diagram or evidence table for oxygen or electron exchange, with the decisive result unmarked.
qrt_instances.independent_check: If a passive coating stops visible lead deposition, does this alone reverse the chemical electron-transfer tendency?

slots.Y: Oxidation and reduction occur together, with oxygen transfer one useful school-level model.
slots.Z: Colour alone is ambiguous. Establish solid identity before and after, characterize the flowing gas and detect water or another oxygen-containing product; constrain hypotheses by atom conservation and reaction conditions.
slots.W: Independently synthesize the decisive model for this exact case: A black solid becomes red after heating in a gas flow. Synthesize evidence needed to decide whether CuO reduction occurred or a different change caused the colour. Check the changed condition: Does a colour change without a change in formal oxidation state automatically count as redox?
